title: billing backfill applied rotated credential IDs to legacy aggregates causing misattributed post-facto charges
creator: Alex Chen
description:
Summary: A scheduled billing backfill job (monthly-usage-reconciler) rehydrating historical aggregates after a shard migration used the live credential-to-org mapping table. Because several customers rotated API keys in Q4 2025, the mapping table contained multiple credential IDs for the same logical account. The backfill logic deduplicated by the current active credential (last-seen) and merged historical rows under that ID, which caused (a) some legacy usage to be attributed to an unrelated rotated key and (b) downstream invoices to include backfilled items for the wrong billing entity.

Impact: Affected ~18 customer orgs across two shard migrations (us-east-1), with invoice previews showing additional line-items totaling ~15k tokens on average for 5 orgs and smaller adjustments for the rest. No guaranteed double-charging yet because invoices are in preview/adjustment; however, customers saw unexpected usage spikes in the Console and in the billing-export downstream.

What happened:
1) During credential rotation customers can have multiple credential IDs associated with the same org (credential_tombstone table retains history).
2) The monthly-usage-reconciler backfill run used credentials.current_owner_lookup JOIN and a GROUP BY credential_id that implicitly favored the most-recent credential id for each historical row.
3) When the historical rows were merged into route/org aggregates, rows were binned by credential_id instead of canonical_org_id, then canonicalization step applied only to the final merged key, which caused some rows to be attributed to the wrong final credential when multiple rotations existed.

Repro steps (local):
- Restore snapshot of shard migration dataset (instructions: s3://redwood-billing-test/snapshots/migration-2025-11).
- Seed credential_tombstone with multiple rotated keys for org A (credential_abc, credential_xyz).
- Run monthly-usage-reconciler with --mode=backfill --date=2025-11-01 and observe merged output in /tmp/usage-merge.csv.
- Confirm that rows originally tagged to credential_abc appear under credential_xyz when rotating order is last-seen=xyz.

Root cause hypothesis: Backfill logic relied on an optimistic assumption that credential IDs are a 1:1 mapping to canonical_org at time-of-usage. The canonicalization was performed after grouping by credential id which allowed out-of-order merges when multiple historical credential ids exist for a single org.

Short-term mitigation (today):
- Disabled scheduled monthly backfill runs for affected shard pools (us-east-1) and set flag backfill.allow_historical_rewrite=false.
- Pushed temporary filter in billing-export to exclude backfill-derived diffs from invoice generation until reconciliation completes.
- Customer outreach: Billing PM notified top-5 customers with largest deltas; Customer Success preparing FAQ and temporary hold on billing previews.

Proposed fixes: (1) Fix backfill to perform canonical_org_id resolution at event-level prior to any GROUP BY/aggregation; (2) Add guarded reconciliation step to verify per-org token-sum invariant before committing aggregates (delta tolerance 0.1%); (3) Extend post-backfill audit that cross-checks pre/post per-org histograms and flags any reassignments > 0.05% for manual review.

Planned rollout: patch in billing-reconciler v2026.03.3 -> run in dry mode for affected window and compare; if results stable, enable commit mode and re-run backfill for the migration window. Target release: billing-2026.03.2 -> 2026-03-17 dry run, 2026-03-20 commit (TBD after dry-run audit).

- Dry-run output (s3): s3://redwood-billing-test/backfill-dryruns/2026-03-14/
